text.p: Arby's Inc parent Triarc Cos Inc sued ZuZu Inc in the Delaware Chancery Court Wednesday seeking mediation in a contract dispute.

The suit is in response to a suit filed by ZuZu in a Dallas state court last month accusing Triarc of alleged unfair competition and of misappropriating information about the "ZuZu Speedy Tortilla", according to court papers made available to Reuters Friday.
The dispute arose from two soured agreements made by the companies in 1995.

In the first, a stock purchase agreement, Triarc paid $5.3 million for a 12.5 percent interest in ZuZu, with the proceeds to be used for stock repurchase by ZuZu and for business development. Triarc alleges in court papers that ZuZu reduced staff and "began experiencing severe financial difficulties almost immediately after the parties entered into the agreement.
In a second agreement on master franchises, the companies arranged an exclusive deal establishing "dual brand locations" in which their two restaurant concepts would operate under one roof.
Triarc said in the lawsuit that its contracts with ZuZu provide for non-binding mediation rather than litigation as the first step in any dispute.

Triarc seeks a court order requiring mediation, an injunction against further action in ZuZu's Dallas lawsuit, and reimbursement for Triarc's "modification" of ZuZu' menu and the salary of a shared employee.
No one at ZuZu could be reached for comment.
